When people see "police officer suspended from duty after ___" they think that's the totality of their punishment, and it's not, it's not even a punishment, it's a part of the investigation process. Suspending a police officer is the first thing they do when an incident occurs so that they don't have a potential criminal working as a law enforcement officer, and to protect the police officer from retaliation, either from civilians or co-workers. The officer has to turn in his gun and badge during the suspension, during working hours he is confined to his home except for medical appointments, dropping off/picking up kids from school, getting food, and other such necessities. He can be called in at any time of day or night to be interviewed and/or interrogated as part of the investigation. They make suspension sound like a vacation, but it's closer to house arrest, with some small leniency. What's surprising in this case is the officer is being suspended without pay. Usually while the officer is under investigation, they are suspended with pay, so as to not punish prematurely punish the officer until the investigation is complete and the findings dictate if and what level of punishment is needed.

Also police officers can be punished judicially (jail, probaton, fines), administratively (fired, demoted, further suspensions), or both depending on the results of the investigation.
